You can go with a consumption based tax (sales tax) paid by the end user of a product or service. Then you just have the vendor collect it as they already do for state/city sales tax. The government would probably collect a lot more money under a system like this.

It is basically a take off of this book by Neal Boortz, called the Fair Tax.

Basically, Boortz wanted to replace income with sales tax - no more withholding. Every month, you get a check for your family's "free" no tax items - the $ you would spend on the tax for $X, so that it wouldn't burden poor people. In fact, it encouraged saving, because the more you save, the less tax you pay.

I believe he set it to a 23% (revenue neutral) rate for everyone. If you spent $1000, you pay $230. If you spent $10,000, you pay $2300. And you got a check for like $250/month/person in "prepaid taxes."

Cruz is saying the same kind of thing, but keeping the income tax. No deductions. Everyone pays 10% after the first $14k/person + $4k/kid in the family (family of 4 making $36k pays no tax). Single mom of 2 pays no taxes on first $22k, but Child tax credit and EITC still in effect, so it works out to about $32k, I believe.

Withholding goes straight to Treasury Dept, and enforcement is easy, because the rules are simple ($INCOME-$36k) * 10% = Taxes due. Taxes due - Tax withheld = Tax overpaid (refund amount) /Tax underpaid (tax owed).

Edit: To answer your question more precisely, businesses would still have to withhold and report income, just like it does today. IRS isn't a collections unit for taxes coming in, it is an enforcement unit to ensure the right amount comes in. It's job is to be the hammer that makes one think twice about putting $200 in charitable donations exemption when you know damn well the thing was only worth $150. In other words, all the rules and regulations and loopholes and exemptions that the IRS is in place to enforce are gone, only leaving the collection part, which is what the Treasury does now, making businesses file using EFTPS (Electronic Federal Tax Payment System.) A business will, for every employee, track their wages, and assess the 10% tax on the expected income amount over $36k (or however you fill out your W-4) if that check were extended out for a full year. They then send that directly to the Treasury department, who keeps track of this also. You then, at the end of the year, get your total wages, subtract off your exemptions ($10k automatic exemption per adult + $4k personal exemption for each household member, including yourself - i.e. family of 4 with 2 parents = $10k + $10k + (4 * $4k) = $36k) your total tax paid, and either pay a little more, or get a little back based on the 10% over the full year. Since there are no loopholes, the Treasury department could just run what amounts to a massive VLOOKUP to find cheaters or under-reporters; hence no need for the IRS.
